questions.question: Which learning approach best develops long-term problem-solving ability in children?

options.text: Limiting questions strictly to the syllabus

questions.explanation: Hands-on experimentation helps children build conceptual understanding and adaptability.

questions.question: When a child makes an unexpected mistake while solving a problem, what is the most constructive response?

options.text: Correct them immediately and give the final answer
Ask open-ended questions to guide them to discover why
Express disappointment so they pay more attention
Switch to an easier task immediately

questions.explanation: Open-ended questions help learners reflect, analyse errors, and build metacognitive skills.

questions.question: In "Education 4.0", technology is primarily seen as:
questions.description: Understanding the role of modern digital tools.

options.text: A tool for children to create, model, and understand real systems
A passive video screen to keep children occupied

questions.explanation: Technology empowers young learners to model real-world phenomena and create original solutions.

questions.question: How can parents best support curiosity in everyday home routines?

options.text: Answer every question with "because I said so"
Investigate everyday phenomena together (e.g. why bread rises)
Discourage taking toys or items apart to see how they work
Rely solely on school homework for all learning

questions.explanation: Exploring simple daily wonders together shows children that learning happens everywhere.

questions.question: What is computational thinking at the foundational level?
questions.description: Thinking skills for the modern age.

options.text: Memorising coding syntax and typing speed
Breaking complex problems into smaller, manageable steps
Spending multiple hours in front of computer screens
Using calculators instead of mental reasoning

questions.explanation: Decomposition, pattern recognition, and step-by-step logic form the core of computational thinking.

questions.question: How does multidisciplinary learning (connecting arts, science, and math) benefit a child?

options.text: It creates holistic thinkers who see real-world connections
It confuses students by mixing unrelated subjects
It should only be introduced at university level
It replaces the need to learn mathematics basics

questions.explanation: Real-world challenges require integrating concepts from science, design, and quantitative reasoning.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to help a child overcome fear of mathematics or science?

options.text: Increase homework drill volume until scores improve
Connect concepts to tangible games, puzzles, and daily life
Compare them with peers who score higher
Avoid discussing math or science altogether

questions.explanation: Puzzles and hands-on activities demystify abstract formulas into joyful, intuitive discoveries.

questions.question: Why is inquiry-based learning important in early education?

options.text: It encourages learners to ask "why" and seek evidence
It ensures all children follow one identical memorised script
It eliminates the need for any guidance or structure
It focuses strictly on exam ranking metrics

questions.explanation: Inquiry-based learning builds independent, critical thinkers capable of evaluating information.

questions.question: What role does creative play have in cognitive development?

options.text: It is a distraction from real educational progress
It develops spatial awareness, collaboration, and experimentation
It is only valuable for physical exercise
It should only be allowed as a reward for high test marks

questions.explanation: Playful experimentation is the foundation upon which children test hypotheses and build resilience.

questions.question: How does encouraging a child to explain a solution in their own words help their mastery?

options.text: It deepens comprehension and reveals gaps in reasoning
It takes too much time compared to reading silent notes
It is only helpful if they use exact book definitions
It has no effect on memory retention

questions.explanation: Articulating reasoning (the Feynman technique) consolidates conceptual understanding.

questions.question: Which colour is a ripe banana?
questions.explanation: A ripe banana is yellow!

questions.question: How many legs does a cat have?
questions.explanation: A cat walks on 4 legs.

questions.question: Which one is round like a ball?
questions.explanation: An orange is round, just like a ball.

questions.question: Which animal says "moo"?
questions.explanation: Cows say moo!

questions.question: What do we use to brush our teeth?
questions.explanation: We brush our teeth with a toothbrush every morning and night.

questions.question: Look at the pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, ___. What comes next?
questions.explanation: We are adding 2 each time: 8 + 2 = 10.

questions.question: Which shape has 3 sides and 3 corners?
questions.explanation: A triangle always has 3 straight sides and 3 corners.

questions.question: A unicorn saw 3 birds on a tree. 2 more birds flew in. How many birds are there now?
questions.explanation: 3 + 2 = 5 birds in total!

questions.question: Which animal lives in water and breathes with gills?
questions.explanation: Fish live in water and use their gills to breathe.

questions.question: Which object will float on water?
questions.explanation: Dry leaves are light and have buoyancy, so they float on water.

questions.question: Which number completes the pattern: 5, 10, 15, 20, ___?
questions.explanation: The pattern increases by 5: 20 + 5 = 25.

questions.question: If a clock shows 3:00, where does the minute hand point?
questions.explanation: At exact hour marks, the minute hand points directly at 12.

questions.question: Which of these is a source of natural light during daytime?
questions.explanation: The Sun is our primary source of natural light and heat.

questions.question: A box has 14 apples. You give 6 apples to friends. How many apples remain in the box?
questions.explanation: 14 - 6 = 8 apples left.

questions.question: Which plant part grows under the ground and absorbs water?
questions.explanation: Roots grow in the soil to absorb water and essential nutrients.

questions.question: What is 7 groups of 4 stars?
questions.explanation: 7 multiplied by 4 equals 28.

questions.question: Which state of water is invisible and present in the air?
questions.explanation: Water vapour is the gaseous, invisible form of water in the atmosphere.

questions.question: A square has sides of 5 cm each. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter of a square = 4 × side length = 4 × 5 = 20 cm.

questions.question: Which direction does the sun rise in the morning?
questions.explanation: Because Earth rotates toward the east, the sun appears to rise in the East.

questions.question: Which fraction is greater than 1/4?
questions.explanation: 1/2 represents two quarters (2/4), which is larger than 1/4.

questions.question: A train travels 60 kilometres in 1 hour. How far does it travel in 3 hours at constant speed?
questions.explanation: Distance = Speed × Time = 60 km/h × 3 h = 180 km.

questions.question: Which simple machine is used in a see-saw playground game?
questions.explanation: A see-saw is a Class 1 lever with the fulcrum in the centre.

questions.question: What is the sum of angles in any triangle?
questions.explanation: The interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180 degrees.

questions.question: Plants make their food using sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water in a process called:
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis transforms solar energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.

questions.question: Which of the following is equivalent to 0.75?
questions.explanation: 3 divided by 4 equals 0.75 (or 75%).

questions.question: Which number completes the pattern: 2, 6, 18, 54, ___?
questions.description: Look at the ratio between adjacent numbers.
questions.explanation: Each term is multiplied by 3: 54 × 3 = 162.

questions.question: What is the boiling point of pure water at standard sea level atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C (212 °F) at sea level pressure.

questions.question: If a rectangle has length 8 cm and width 5 cm, what is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of rectangle = Length × Width = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

questions.question: Which gas is most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up approximately 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question: A robot turns 90° clockwise, then 180° clockwise. How many degrees total did it turn?
questions.explanation: 90° + 180° = 270° clockwise rotation.

questions.question: What is the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24... Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24... The smallest common is 24.

questions.question: What happens to the shadow of a flagpole as midday (solar noon) approaches?

options.text: It disappears completely all year round

questions.explanation: As the sun rises higher overhead toward noon, cast shadows become shorter.

questions.question: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration, powering cellular activities.

questions.question: In an electric circuit, what component opens or closes the flow of electric current?
questions.explanation: A switch bridges or breaks the conductive path in an electric circuit.

questions.question: If the ratio of boys to girls in a robotics club is 3:2, and there are 15 boys, how many girls are there?
questions.explanation: 15 / 3 = 5 multiplier. 5 × 2 = 10 girls.

questions.question: What is the value of x in the equation: 3x - 7 = 14?
Lemon juice tastes sour and turns blue litmus red. This indicates it is:
questions.explanation: Acids have a sour taste and turn blue litmus paper red (citric acid in lemons).

questions.question: A cyclist rides 36 km/h. How many metres does the cyclist travel in 1 second?
Heat transfer through vacuum (such as sunlight reaching Earth) occurs via:
questions.explanation: Radiation transmits thermal energy via electromagnetic waves without requiring a material medium.

questions.question: What is the sum of any two supplementary angles?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles always sum to 180 degrees.

questions.question: What is the square root of 196?
Friction between moving engine parts is generally reduced using:
questions.explanation: Lubricants form a smooth micro-layer between sliding surfaces to minimize friction and wear.

questions.question: The binary number 1010 in base 10 (decimal) is equal to:
questions.explanation: 8 + 0 + 2 + 0 = 10 in decimal.

questions.question: Sound cannot travel through which of the following?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical pressure wave that requires a material medium to propagate.

questions.question: If 4 workers can build a prototype in 6 days, how many days will 8 workers take at the same pace?
questions.explanation: Inverse proportion: 4 × 6 = 24 worker-days. 24 / 8 = 3 days.

questions.question: Newton’s First Law of Motion is also widely known as the Law of:
questions.explanation: Newton’s first law states an object remains in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by a net external force.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of work and energy?
questions.explanation: Work and energy are measured in Joules (1 Joule = 1 Newton-metre).

questions.question: What are the roots of the quadratic equation x² - 5x + 6 = 0?
The atomic number of an element is determined by the number of:

options.text: Electrons in its outer shell only

questions.explanation: Atomic number (Z) uniquely identifies an element by the count of protons in its nucleus.

questions.question: In coordinate geometry, in which quadrant does the point (-4, 5) lie?
questions.explanation: Quadrant II has negative x and positive y coordinates.

questions.question: According to Ohm's law, if voltage across a resistor doubles while resistance remains constant, the current:
questions.explanation: V = I × R. When V doubles at constant R, current I must also double.

questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm produces a real image of the same size as the object when the object is placed at:
questions.explanation: At 2F (twice the focal length = 40 cm), a convex lens forms an inverted, real image of identical height at 2F on the opposite side.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of rust on iron?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide: Fe2O3 · xH2O.

questions.question: What is the probability of rolling a prime number on a standard fair six-sided die?
questions.explanation: Prime numbers on a die are 2, 3, and 5 (3 outcomes out of 6) = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.question: Which hereditary material carries genetic instructions in living organisms?
questions.explanation: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) stores genetic codes across biological generations.

questions.question: Two vectors of magnitude 3 N and 4 N act at a right angle (90°) to each other. What is their resultant magnitude?
According to the First Law of Thermodynamics, ΔU = Q - W. What does ΔU represent?

options.text: Change in internal energy of the system

questions.explanation: ΔU represents the internal energy change resulting from heat added minus work performed.

questions.question: What is the derivative of f(x) = x³ - 4x + 7 with respect to x?
questions.explanation: d/dx (x³) = 3x², d/dx (-4x) = -4, and d/dx (7) = 0. Result: 3x² - 4.

questions.question: Which quantum number primarily determines the energy and size of an atomic orbital?
questions.explanation: The principal quantum number n defines the principal electron shell and overall energy scale.

questions.question: In Python programming, which data structure is ordered and immutable?
questions.explanation: Tuples maintain insertion order and cannot be mutated after initial creation.

questions.question: What is the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor directly proportional to?
questions.explanation: C = εA/d. Capacitance is directly proportional to plate surface area A.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integral ∫ from 0 to 2 of (3x²) dx:
questions.explanation: ∫ 3x² dx = x³. Evaluated from 0 to 2: 2³ - 0³ = 8.

questions.question: Which phenomenon provides definitive evidence for the wave nature of light?
questions.explanation: Interference and diffraction patterns (as in Young’s double-slit experiment) prove wave characteristics.

questions.question: In digital logic, which gate outputs 0 ONLY when both inputs are 1?
questions.explanation: A NAND gate is the inverse of AND: it outputs 0 if and only if both inputs are 1.

questions.question: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is 10 days. After 30 days, what fraction of the original sample remains?
questions.explanation: 30 days = 3 half-lives. Remaining fraction = (1/2)³ = 1/8.

questions.question: What is the average-case time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL / Red-Black)?
questions.explanation: Balanced BSTs halve the search space at each branch, yielding logarithmic time O(log n).

questions.question: In relational database theory, what does the "A" in ACID transaction guarantees represent?
questions.explanation: Atomicity ensures that all operations within a transaction succeed together or are completely rolled back.

questions.question: Which machine learning concept describes a model learning noise and idiosyncrasies of training data instead of generalising?
questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when high model complexity memorises training noise, damaging test generalization.

questions.question: In systems architecture, what does Amdahl's law quantify?

options.text: The theoretical speedup limit of parallel computing constrained by serial portions
The doubling of transistors on microchips every two years
Network latency proportional to physical transmission distance
Disk input-output throughput saturation in database clusters

questions.explanation: Amdahl’s law defines the maximum theoretical speedup achievable via parallel processors for a workload.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental pillar of Education 4.0 in engineering and science disciplines?

options.text: Memorising legacy reference handbooks without questioning principles
Interdisciplinary cyber-physical problem solving and experimental iteration
Treating hardware and software as completely isolated fields
Standardised paper tests as the sole assessment metric

questions.explanation: Education 4.0 prepares modern professionals through rapid prototyping, data-driven reasoning, and interconnected systems.

questions.question: What is the philosophy of Unicorn Learning Lab in Education 4.0?
questions.explanation: Our philosophy "Think. Explore. Discover." encourages children to question, experiment, and learn joyfully.

questions.question: What is 5 + 7 in mental arithmetic?
Which of the following is an example of an input device in computing?
questions.explanation: Keyboards and mice send input signals into the computing system.

questions.question: Which natural satellite orbits planet Earth?
questions.explanation: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

questions.question: In Education 4.0, what is the best way to handle a design mistake during a project?

options.text: Analyse what happened, adjust the design, and test again

questions.explanation: Iterative testing and learning from errors is the heart of scientific inquiry and engineering.
